texts: mixed: the frost, the coming and the date all come through, but "first" is recorded against the frost's own class instead of against the coming, so a question like "which frost came first?" cannot match it; the fix is to state the rank as an explicit "the first ... to V". Rewrite: "On day 92 of Year 1, a hard frost came, and it was the first hard frost to come." Separately, "day 92 of Year 1" has no exact slot in the date vocabulary and lands in the day-of-month position, so two such dates cannot be ordered against each other — no rewrite avoids that unless the calendar gains a month-like unit.
good. the being-white is reified so both "with rime" and "in the morning" attach to it, and the plain "the harbor was white" fact is kept alongside.
good. the wind, its coldness, the sea as origin and the dusk-to-dawn span are all carried, with the blowing treated as something the wind undergoes rather than does deliberately.
good. parses as a fireable per-lantern rule restricted to lanterns on the Cliff Path, with the salt-bloom and each lantern's own mire-essence both covered.

bad: "the mire-essence" has no referent the parse can reach back to — the previous sentence gives each lantern its own mire-essence inside a universal rule, and a later bare definite cannot point into a rule like that, so the parse mints a fresh, unrelated mire-essence and the burning ends up detached from the lanterns entirely. Repeat the quantifier so the burning is stated per lantern: "In every lantern on the Cliff Path, the mire-essence burned slowly."
good. parses as a fireable per-lantern rule, keeping the staying-lit continuation, the dusk-to-dawn span and the Cliff Path restriction.
